title: Release Gate: traffic-split pinning and performance snapshot explorer
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Teams onboarding new model versions need a single console flow to (1) select a target model/version, (2) pin a percentage of traffic (traffic-split pinning) or fully anchor production routes, and (3) immediately inspect pre-published performance snapshots and profiles so they can decide whether to promote or roll back. Current Console flows require multiple pages: a version list, separate pin configuration, and a disconnected performance profile explorer. This creates risk (misconfigured pins), slows rollouts, and prevents quick guardrail checks before deployment.

Proposal summary: Add a unified "Release Gate" flow in the Console that surfaces: a compact model/version chooser, an inline traffic-split slider with advanced mode for canary rules, and a contextual performance snapshot panel showing latency P50/P95, token cost estimates, sample traces, and profile badges (e.g., quantized, batched, GPU kernel family). The snapshot panel should show the published profile used for prior runs and any recent profile regression alerts. The flow enables pin-by-traffic (0-100%), immediate dry-run simulation of expected cost/latency, and a one-click promote/rollback CTA.

Scope: UX and frontend Console changes to add the Release Gate modal and snapshot panel; backend API changes to return published performance profiles and simulate expected economics for traffic-split; telemetry events for auditing traffic-split changes; and a minimal guardrail that prevents >50% traffic pin without an SLA or owner approval (configurable). This ticket captures the PM surface and acceptance criteria; engineering and design tasks are surfaced in dependent tickets.

Design constraints and considerations: keep the primary flow keyboard-accessible and mobile-responsive at narrow widths in the Console; performance snapshot queries must be cached with a 30s TTL to avoid spiky load; simulate mode must be read-only and labeled clearly. Profile metadata must include model hash, quantization level, typical sequence length percentile used for cost estimates, and last-run timestamp.

Metrics for success: 30% reduction in average time-to-pin for new model releases; less than 1% misconfigured pins reported in support tickets in the first quarter after launch; 80%+ of release decisions use the snapshot explorer before promoting in pilot teams.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows a Release Gate flow accessible from model details and from the Versions table
Within the flow, users can select a model version and set a traffic split (0-100%) via slider or numeric input
Advanced mode allows scheduling a canary ramp and adding a single fallback rule
Performance snapshot panel displays the latest published profile for the chosen version, including latency P50/P95, token cost estimate, quantization, and last-run timestamp
Simulate button returns an estimated cost and median latency for the requested traffic-split and expected sequence length (uses cached profile data)
Audit event emitted for every pin change with actor, timestamp, from/to percentages, and note (if provided)
Guardrail prevents setting >50% traffic-split without owner approval; owner approval flow triggers an approver email/console notification
One-click promote upgrades a pinned split to 100% and records a release note; one-click rollback restores previous split and attaches the rollback reason
Automated e2e test covers the happy path: open Release Gate, set 10% canary, simulate, promote, and rollback
Documentation and in-console microcopy explain 'simulate' vs 'dry-run' and how cost estimates are computed
